title: Gatekeeper: adaptive rollout translator for environment-aware canaries and shadowing
creator: Jared Kim
description: Implement a Gatekeeper service that translates canonical rollout policies (canary percentages, A/B splits, shadowing, auto-rollback thresholds) into environment-specific traffic controls for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The Gatekeeper will enforce environment constraints (capacity, network egress, tenant isolation) and produce an executable routing plan that the control plane and edge proxies can apply.
rationale: Current rollout tooling assumes a single uniform execution model. Differences in capacity guarantees (Dedicated), network topology and control-plane reachability (Private), and multi-tenant pooling (Hosted) cause repeated manual adjustments and safety gaps during model promotion. Gatekeeper centralizes policy synthesis and emits environment-aware manifests so we can run the same high-level experiment across modes with predictable safety and cost behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Gatekeeper accepts a canonical rollout manifest and emits per-environment routing plans (hosted/dedicated/private) with explicit traffic allocations and admission rules
Control plane integration: hosted control plane accepts Gatekeeper plan via /apply-rollout and actuates traffic splits in runtime (validated in staging)
Dedicated: plan includes capacity reservations and a conservative admission controller that rejects steps exceeding reserved throughput estimates
Private: plan produces an offline bundle (signed JSON) that on-prem control-plane adapter can validate and apply without outbound control-plane reachability
Auto-rollback hooks wired: metrics thresholds (latency p95, error-rate, model-quality regressions) trigger automated rollback actions and are testable in canary staging
Observability: rollout dashboard shows planned vs actual traffic, hold durations, and rollback events for each environment
E2E tests: synthetic canary run across all three environments demonstrating staged exposure, shadowing, and an automated rollback triggered by injected latency regression

2026-03-07: Spike completed to enumerate environment capabilities; measured median slot throughput for dedicated pools and control plane latency for private adapters (notes attached)

2026-03-09: Prototype translator implemented that converts a canonical canary manifest into hosted routing rules and a standalone private bundle (github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-gatekeeper/pull/112)
2026-03-11: Design review with SRE and Platform; agreed to add a resource-aware admission controller for Dedicated and a signed-bundle workflow for Private

decisions: Use a single canonical rollout manifest format (yaml/json) with templating for environment variables rather than three separate formats

Gatekeeper will perform conservative capacity estimation rather than exact allocation for Dedicated to avoid noisy capacity overcommit; Dedicated reservations are advisory and admitted only if static capacity checks pass
Private deployments will receive signed, versioned bundles and a small validation shim will run locally to ensure plan compatibility with on-prem constraints
Shadow traffic will be implemented as passive mirroring to avoid billing surprises in Dedicated; for Hosted we will support billed shadowing with opt-in flags
Auto-rollback thresholds are pluggable policies: default set to p95 latency +20% sustained 5m, error-rate +0.8% absolute 3m, model-quality regression with eval set AUC drop >3% on canary prompts
open_questions: How granular should resource-aware admission be for multi-tenant Dedicated pools (per-tenant reservations vs. pool-leveraged headroom)?
For Private bundles: what is the minimal metadata required for audits without leaking cloud-side telemetry?
Should shadow traffic in Dedicated ever be billed by default (cost vs. fidelity trade-off)?
How to express model-quality regression policies so they can be evaluated for non-differentiable outputs (use eval harness + human-in-loop alerts)?
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Shadow-only for 30m with sampling 1% of traffic (hosted: mirrored requests to model-canary; dedicated/private: passive capture without token charge where possible)
Stage 1: Canary ramp: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with hold times [10m, 20m, 30m, 60m] respectively
Stage 2: Concurrent A/B for feature gating: split test at 50/50 for 1 hour on a small subset of tenants (opt-in labels)
Stage 3: Full promotion with rollback guard active for 24h and quality monitoring on lagging evals
Dedicated adjustments: each step includes a pre-check that compares required RPS with reserved capacity estimates; if pre-check fails, Gatekeeper lowers step target or aborts
Private adjustments: operator must manually approve the bundle if the deployment cannot reach the central control plane; Gatekeeper indicates the required operator action in the bundle
rollback_criteria: Latency: p95 increases by >20% vs baseline for 5 continuous minutes
Errors: 5xx rate above 1% absolute for 3 continuous minutes OR error-rate increases by >200% vs baseline
Quality: eval harness detects AUC/accuracy drop >3% on the canonical prompt set within canary window
Operational: GPU OOMs or scheduler rejections observed during the stage
Manual: on-call triggers emergency rollback with a one-click control plane action
environment_constraints: Hosted: elastic pooled capacity, supports dynamic traffic shifts, billing per-token; can perform billed shadowing; control plane fully reachable
Dedicated: reserved capacity, strict throughput guarantees, change windows may apply; prefer conservative admissions to prevent tenant interference
Private: may be air-gapped; control-plane operations require signed bundles and Operator approval; cannot assume telemetry ingestion — Gatekeeper must embed offline validation rules
config_parity_notes: Canonical manifest maps to per-environment feature flags: e.g., 'shadowing:billed' toggles across environments
Quantization/variant fallback: Gatekeeper will annotate plans with compatible fallback model variants when memory or accelerator mismatch is detected
Timeouts and retry semantics: reduced retry budgets for Dedicated to avoid overload, increased for Private to tolerate network variance
Secrets and KMS: Private bundles should reference consumer KMS paths rather than cloud-managed URIs; Gatekeeper will include a placeholder schema
test_plan: Unit tests for translator logic covering environment substitution and capacity heuristics
Simulated cluster in CI that applies Gatekeeper plan and asserts admission decisions under synthetic load
Canary E2E with staging hosted account: run full ramp and inject latency to verify auto-rollback
Dedicated lab run against a reserved GPU pool with resource pressure injection to validate admission controller
Private bundle dry-run with an operator in lab environment to validate signed-bundle apply and offline validator
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on the capacity estimation heuristics and the Private signed-bundle format. Ensure the rollback thresholds are realistic for high-throughput tenants and that the observability hooks expose per-tenant deltas for A/B runs.
